title: Staying on Course: Three-Year Results of the National Guard Youth ChalleNGe Evaluation
design: Random assignment in 10 sites; outcomes measured about three years after study entry.
population: Youth ages 16–18 who were out of school and unemployed, eligible for the intensive residential program.
delivery: Two-week orientation, 20-week residential phase, then one year of postresidential mentoring.

findings.unit: percentage-point difference, three years after random assignment

limits: The evaluation’s high-intensity residential model and out-of-school youth population are not comparable to ordinary K–12 classroom interventions. Do not infer effects for all young people, all sites, or current program delivery. Keep source-year currency unresolved rather than assigning a price year.
